newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures failed to hang onto their gains after a favourable U.S. consumer price report and drifted lower to end little changed ahead of key German economic reports due later this week.
Traders said the market lacked direction and although most remained bullish for the medium-term there was a risk of a short-term correction given the gains of the past week.
Analysts said the German M3 money supply report and Ifo business climate survey, both due this week, would be the main focus for the bond market.
"There wasn't much excitement today, (U.S.) inflation was much better than expected, but there was little reaction," Philippe Brossard, head of research at ABN Amro in Paris said.
"The focus has turned more to forex with the lira battle and the dollar problem...and this week we still have the German numbers. People are in a wait-and-see mood."
The March bond future rallied to 132.86 after the inflation numbers, close to the historic high of 132.94 touched on Tuesday, but slipped back to 132.62, down 0.06 on the day.
Several traders said there was a chance of further declines, perhaps to 131.50, to fill gaps left during last week's rally.

Traders said the comments from Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer, aimed at halting the rise of the dollar against the mark, had been one of the reasons for the selloff in French interest rate futures early on Wednesday.
The comments had further dampened any lingering hopes of reductions in German interest rates anytime soon.
March PIBOR recovered from an early selloff, which sent it as low as 96.64, but June was left languishing down five basis points at 96.68.

Brossard said France appeared to be relatively immune from the growing EMU jitters in other European countries, sparked by doubts about Germany's ability to hit deficit targets and the chance of a standoff with Italy about entry in the first wave.
"In France, concern is very low. There is more talk about it, but the French don't believe the Germans can delay," he said.
The franc recovered from an early drop to trade little changed at 3.3782 against the mark after touching a low of 3.3801.
